mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 2% and S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in the last three months signals a tightening labor market, which is typically associated with increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5% in 3 months and S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases for three consecutive months and S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last month signals increased economic activity, which is typically associated with higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases by more than 1% in 1 month and S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 70% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds the historical average by more than 1%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds the historical average by more than 1% and S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) and Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% each in the last two months signals a strong demand environment, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 5% in 2 months
failure_condition: If both HOUST and RSAFS increase by more than 5% in 2 months and S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in the last month, combined with a decrease in the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a robust labor market, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3% in 1 month and S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in the last three months signals a contraction in economic activity, which is typically associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases by more than 2% in 3 months and S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases, the hypothesis fails.
